---
title: "Week 11: Deaths of Despair"
---

## Theme: The Opioid Crisis: Structural Causes, Settlement Law, and
Treatment Deserts

The opioid epidemic\'s geography tracks disinvestment, unemployment, and
despair with remarkable precision. Ohio has been one of the hardest-hit
states --- and a leader in legal settlements requiring data-justified
resource allocation. This week we map treatment \'deserts\' and build an
interactive R-Shiny dashboard for stakeholder engagement.

## Classroom Lab Demonstration

**Legal Focus:** Opioid settlement law and fiduciary responsibility; the
legal requirement for states to spend settlement funds on \'abatement\'
(direct harm reduction) rather than general government purposes; how
epidemiological data and spatial analysis are used to satisfy legal
burden-of-proof standards in settlement fund allocation decisions.

**Health Focus:** Geographic access to medication for opioid use
disorder (MOUD --- buprenorphine, methadone, naltrexone) as a social
determinant of overdose mortality; treatment \'deserts\' defined as
areas with overdose rates above the county median AND drive-time to
nearest MOUD provider exceeding 30 minutes.

**Data:** NVDRS (National Violent Death Reporting System) overdose
mortality data --- restricted use; Ohio overdose mortality data provided
on Carmen from Ohio Department of Health (odh.ohio.gov); SAMHSA
Treatment Locator MOUD provider data (findtreatment.gov/api ---
pre-downloaded CSV on Carmen); CDC SVI 2020.

**R Code:** osrm::osrmIsochrone() to compute drive-time isochrones
around each MOUD provider (30-minute radius); sf::st_join() to identify
census tracts within 30-minute drive of a provider; dplyr::case_when()
to classify tracts as treatment deserts; shiny::fluidPage(),
shiny::sliderInput(), renderPlot() for interactive Shiny app.

- Load Ohio overdose mortality data (provided on Carmen) and SAMHSA MOUD
  provider locations

- Calculate 30-minute drive-time isochrones around each MOUD provider
  using osrm::osrmIsochrone()

- Identify census tracts with overdose rates above county median AND
  outside all 30-min provider isochrones --- these are treatment deserts

- Build a basic R-Shiny app displaying the treatment desert map with a
  slider for drive-time threshold (15, 30, 45, 60 minutes) and SVI
  overlay toggle
